prompt.context: Our client is a defense technology firm that designs and manufactures classified advanced systems, and is headquartered in Boston, with locations throughout the US. Due to economic pressure and competitive threats, profits are declining and the firm is looking for ways to reduce spending. The primary area of interest is evaluating their options for transporting executives from headquarters to their various offices throughout the US.
prompt.question: The firm has hired you to outline their business travel options. What do you recommend?

clarifying_info.q: How many offices does the firm have, and where are they located?
clarifying_info.a: Three key cities: New York, Chicago, and San Francisco.

clarifying_info.q: How often do executives travel to each location?
clarifying_info.a: New York: 2 meetings/week; Chicago: 2 meetings/week; San Francisco: 1 meeting/week. Assume 50 weeks/year.

clarifying_info.q: How many passengers travel per trip?
clarifying_info.a: New York flights: 10 passengers; Chicago flights: 12 passengers; San Francisco flights: 10 passengers.

clarifying_info.q: What is the one-way distance to each city?
clarifying_info.a: New York: 250 miles; Chicago: 1,000 miles; San Francisco: 2,500 miles.

clarifying_info.q: What are the current commercial airline costs?
clarifying_info.a: JFK round-trip ticket: $600 (100 flights/year, 10 passengers = $600K). ORD round-trip ticket: $1,000 (100 flights/year, 12 passengers = $1,200K). SFO round-trip ticket: $1,400 (50 flights/year, 10 passengers = $700K). Total: $2,500K/year.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a partnership option with a commercial airline?
clarifying_info.a: Yes. An airline partnership would yield 20% savings, reducing total cost to $2,000K/year.

clarifying_info.q: What private plane lease options are available?
clarifying_info.a: Small jet: range 2,000 mi, capacity 10, speed 400 mi/hr, cost $1.0K/hr. Medium jet: range 3,000 mi, capacity 12, speed 500 mi/hr, cost $2.0K/hr. Large jet: range 4,000 mi, capacity 14, speed 600 mi/hr, cost $2.4K/hr.

clarifying_info.q: What does it cost to buy a private plane?
clarifying_info.a: $20M for a 10-year utilization period. Plane cost represents 66.67% of total annual cost, so total annual cost is $3M/year.

exhibits.title: Annual Costs of Leasing and Buying Jet
exhibits.shows: Two stacked 100% bar charts side by side. The left bar shows the cost breakdown for a Leased Jet; the right bar shows the cost breakdown for a Private (Purchased) Plane. Each bar is divided into colored segments representing different cost categories as a percentage of total annual cost.

data.leased_jet_note: Lease cost = 80% of total leased cost
data.private_plane_note: Plane cost = 66.67% of total purchase cost

framework: Utilization: number of trips, offices served, passengers per flight, annual mileage
Transportation Options: commercial airline, airline partnership, lease private plane, buy private plane
Cost of Each Option: airfare, lease fees, fuel, maintenance, crew, hangar/garage, insurance
Other Factors: productivity, confidentiality/privacy, scheduling flexibility, risk of delays

questions.prompt: What do you need to know about the firm's transportation utilization?
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask about number of offices, trip frequency, passenger counts, and distances. Strong answer quantifies total annual flights and miles traveled to set up the cost comparison.

questions.prompt: What are the options for transporting executives to meetings?
questions.guidance: Four options: (1) Commercial airline, (2) Partnership with commercial airline (20% discount), (3) Lease a private plane, (4) Buy a private plane. Candidate should identify all four before moving to cost calculation.

questions.prompt: Calculate the cost of the commercial airline option.
questions.guidance: Use the utilization data and per-ticket costs provided to sum annual ticket spend across all three routes.

math.setup: Flights/year × passengers/flight = tickets/year; tickets/year × RT ticket cost = annual cost per route. Sum across routes.

questions.prompt: Of the leasing options, which plane size would you choose, and what is the lease cost?
questions.guidance: Candidate must screen out small jet (range 2,000 mi insufficient for SFO at 2,500 mi; capacity 10 insufficient for ORD needing 12 passengers). Medium and large jets both work operationally. Cost per mile is $4 for both. Total miles drives total lease cost.

math.setup: Total round-trip miles = sum of (flights/year × 2 × one-way distance) for each route. Lease cost = $4/mi × total miles.
steps: Lease cost = 80% of total cost → Total cost = $2,000K / 0.80 = $2,500K/year
math.answer: $2,500K/year for either medium or large jet

questions.prompt: What other costs are associated with the leasing and buying options?
questions.guidance: For leasing: fuel, maintenance, crew (exhibit shows these as the non-lease portion, ~20% of total). For buying: all leasing costs PLUS hangar/garage and insurance (exhibit shows plane cost is 66.67% of total, leaving ~33.33% for other costs). Candidate should read the exhibit to identify all cost buckets.

questions.prompt: What is the total annual cost of the buying option?
questions.guidance: Plane cost of $20M over 10 years = $2M/year amortized. Plane cost represents 66.67% of total annual cost.

math.setup: Annual plane cost = $20M / 10 years = $2M. Plane cost = 66.67% of total → Total = $2M / 0.6667

questions.prompt: What do you recommend: commercial airline, leasing, or buying?
questions.guidance: Buying is ~20% more expensive than commercial or leasing ($3M vs $2.5M). Commercial and leasing have identical costs at $2.5M/year, but leasing is preferable because it offers productivity gains, privacy/confidentiality (important for a defense firm), scheduling flexibility, and no risk of commercial delays.

questions.prompt: Given the airline partnership savings of 20%, would you change your recommendation?
questions.guidance: Partnership reduces commercial cost to $2M/year, which is $500K/year cheaper than leasing. However, the same qualitative advantages of leasing (productivity, privacy, flexibility, no delay risk) still apply. More research is needed to understand whether the $500K saving outweighs those benefits for a defense firm that values confidentiality.

brainstorming.prompt: What other costs are associated with the leasing and buying options beyond the base lease or purchase price?

categories.name: Qualitative / Hidden Costs
ideas: Productivity value of time saved vs. commercial
Confidentiality risk on commercial flights (defense firm)
Exposure to commercial airline delays and cancellations

recommendation: Recommend leasing a large private jet at $2,500K/year, identical in cost to commercial airline but superior on qualitative dimensions critical to a defense technology firm: executive productivity, confidentiality of classified work discussions, scheduling flexibility, and elimination of commercial delay risk.
Choose the large jet over the medium jet: same cost per mile ($4/mi), but faster (600 mi/hr vs. 500 mi/hr) and higher capacity (14 vs. 12), providing buffer for larger delegations.
Do not buy: $3M/year is 20% above both commercial and leasing options with only one plane available, creating single-point-of-failure risk.
risks: Airline partnership at $2M/year saves $500K annually vs. leasing; if confidentiality and flexibility are less critical than assumed, partnership may be preferable
Leasing locks the firm into a contract; demand fluctuations (e.g., office closures) could make the fixed cost structure unfavorable
Single leased plane creates scheduling bottlenecks if multiple simultaneous trips are needed
next_steps: Conduct deeper analysis of the firm's confidentiality requirements and sensitivity of executive travel discussions
Evaluate partnership terms in detail (scheduling restrictions, upgrade options, any exclusivity clauses)
Model scenarios where travel volume changes ±20% to assess cost sensitivity
Assess whether a two-plane strategy (medium + small backup) is warranted for scheduling resilience
